reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a pre-launch program in which $99 in Bitcoin secures a binary position, and an additional pool-unit purchase is required to obtain a referral link. The pitch ties commissions to referred purchases and describes a founders’ pool share of mined coins using prospective daily earnings examples, not realized payouts.

in order to get a referral link, so that you can referral others, you're going to need to purchase at least one unit. So you'll need to do the $99 in bitcoin. And you'll need to do at least one unit in the $500 pool or the $1,000 pool or the $2,000 pool
the remainder part of that is going to do what is going to purchase computer equipment on computer speed
if you're in the $500 pool you'll be able to purchase fractional units of the $500 pool
You have to be one of the first five hundred spots where you get a unit in each of the three pools so the five hundred dollar pool the hundred the thousand dollar pool the two thousand dollar pool

opening.argument: The presentation uses material uncertainty rather than a guarantee. The speaker expressly tells viewers not to hurt themselves financially, acknowledges that Bitcoin could be worth less or more, and says he has no idea where its price will go. He also explains that daily payouts will not begin immediately and warns viewers to expect a delay. That is a conditional, risk-aware discussion of a volatile cryptocurrency opportunity, not a representation that returns are certain. The numerical illustration is presented as an example tied to assumptions, while the speaker explicitly distinguishes the example from what will happen at launch.

citations.quote: If you don't have the resources, then you don't have the resources. Don't hurt yourself.
Bitcoin could be less than that. It's less than that is less than that today.
I have no idea okay of where that's going to be.
don't expect daily payouts to begin right away

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $99 and pool language establishes an entry structure, but it does not establish a guaranteed return. The speaker expressly says payouts are delayed, describes commissions as subject to Bitcoin verification, and qualifies the mining projection by saying the operation will not begin at the example scale. Those qualifications materially change how the figures should be read: as conditional forecasts with disclosed uncertainty, not promises of realized earnings.

citations.quote: the daily payouts are still going to be a couple of weeks away
the transactions have to be verified through the Bitcoin network system
Do we expect to come out the gate Mining 900 coins a day? The answer is absolutely not

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not erase the proposed paid-return mechanism. The speaker still ties a $99 payment to a binary position, requires pool purchases for referral access, and presents a founders’ share of mined coins. The uncertainty concerns timing and Bitcoin price, while the underlying offer remains a solicitation for money in exchange for prospective mining-linked payouts.

The founders pool, how do you become a founder?

opening.argument: This is best understood as an operational briefing and educational webinar about how participants would use the proposed system. The speaker explains how a recorded webinar can be shared, how referral links are expected to work, how Bitcoin transactions are confirmed, and where viewers can research wallets and exchanges. He also describes a future webinar whose stated purpose is helping people connect with their referral links and get started. Explaining workflow, timing, verification, and wallet options is instructional content; the video does not document completed payouts or demonstrate that any claimed result has occurred.

the transactions have to be verified through the Bitcoin network system
Bitcoin.org is another great resource for you to start researching wallets and vaults.
the purpose of the webinar would be to help people make sure that they are connected with the people in terms of their referral links

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of instructions does not make the subject matter a solicitation. The video explains anticipated launch logistics, transaction confirmation, wallet research, and how to locate a referrer. Its practical focus is helping an audience navigate a planned system and webinar, while the supplied material does not establish that the speaker is showing a completed payout or certifying an outcome.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructions are not neutral technical education: they tell viewers what to pay and what purchase is needed to obtain a referral link. The speaker also instructs viewers to send referral links to personal lists and describes commissions from referred purchases. Operational detail can make a solicitation easier to follow; it does not change the paid recruitment and prospective-return substance.

we're going to be sending out our referral link to our personal list
referral commissions paid out to you in Bitcoin

opening.argument: The evidence can also be read as promotion of a proposed service with ordinary purchases, pools, and referral administration, rather than proof of a scam mechanism. The speaker describes different pool units, explains that commissions can be withdrawn or reused, and says the company intends to purchase computer equipment. He does not show a completed transaction, request passwords or account credentials, or establish that any payout has occurred. Indeed, he admits he has not seen the back end. The record therefore shows a pre-launch commercial proposal whose operation and results remain unverified, not an established fraudulent outcome.

citations.quote: the remainder part of that is going to do what is going to purchase computer equipment
Another option is you can withdraw to your own Bitcoin e wallet
I've not seen the back end of anything at this point

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the pools and referral process ordinary commerce does not require assuming safety; it simply identifies what the supplied evidence actually proves. The speaker describes purchases, commissions, and equipment funding, but the record does not establish that money was taken deceptively, that credentials were requested, or that a payout failed. The prosecution's interpretation depends on treating a proposed structure as proof of fraud.

citations.quote: the company's not taking that revenue and paying that out daily
I've not seen the back end of anything at this point

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is the mechanism being promoted, not whether a completed loss is shown. The speaker makes payment necessary to secure a binary spot and to obtain referral access, then links pool participation to commissions and mined-coin distributions. The proposed computer equipment does not independently verify mining, and the absence of a demonstrated loss cannot turn a paid, recruitment-dependent return scheme into ordinary commerce.
